checkpointLeaseFollowUp.mode: Real disposable PostgreSQL schemas and local Python/Java execution; the two lease regressions model 75 seconds of remote elapsed time under a configured 60-second lease without a wall-clock wait or live cloud calls
coverage: PBL manual and maintenance checkpoints protect the lease before source snapshot I/O
Generic workspace saves renew within their existing environment lock before idle/export work
Checkpoint renewal requests the longer of the configured lifetime and the shared deadline plus 60 seconds
Ordinary provider renewal never shortens a longer remaining lease
Failed, stalled or expired checkpoint renewal cannot start export, commit a checkpoint or release the environment
Late ownership lookup after cancellation cannot start a provider timeout update
checkpointLeaseFollowUp.selfReview: Targeted subagent re-review found no new confirmed lease, deadline, lock or authorization regression; expired-grace and discard paths remain unchanged.

sourceDeadlineFollowUp.mode: Controlled SDK I/O and real disposable PostgreSQL schemas with local Python/Java execution; no additional cloud compute allocated
coverage: Source enumeration and file reads propagate the shared signal through service/provider boundaries and both provider connections
Stalled ownership lookup, connection, source copy, download, stream and cleanup cannot retain the caller after the shared deadline
Existing local 30-second stream timeout remains effective with a longer live Agent signal
Pre-expired requests start no provider I/O and late copy results cannot start downloads
Ignored adapter cancellation releases study admission, preserves the previous checkpoint and cannot overwrite a later checkpoint with late file/list results
Deferred-archive regression waits for later scans rather than assuming exact next-scan admission order
sourceDeadlineFollowUp.selfReview: Targeted subagent review confirmed both connection stages, enumeration, local timeout composition and bounded cleanup; no new confirmed issue. Races remain limited to read-only/provider I/O.

maintenanceAdmissionFollowUp.mode: Real disposable PostgreSQL schemas and local Python/Java execution with controlled provider/model behavior; no additional cloud compute allocated
coverage: Reproduced unrelated activity failing with PBL_BUSY while two maintenance exports occupied the default pool's two study slots
Slow maintenance leaves admission for unrelated activity and commands across LearningStore instances sharing a pool
Deferred idle archive finishes on a subsequent scan
Queued/running Agent, recent reading, non-overdue commands and recent command/Agent completions retain lease protection during admission contention
Idle/overdue-only studies, expired archive grace and durable discard intent do not receive deferred lease renewal
Lease-only protection does not change teaching revisions or learner activity timestamps
maintenanceAdmissionFollowUp.selfReview: Reviewer identified lease starvation from fully serial scans and renewal after discard intent; final diff preserves both scan workers, adds bounded lease-only protection and checks discard intent. Re-review found no remaining confirmed issue.

inputAndBootValidationFollowUp.selfReview: Targeted subagent review found no confirmed new defect in activity coalescing, scene cleanup or fatal boot validation

observations: Scene return restored the exact acknowledged file
Visible idle polling did not reallocate reclaimed compute
Fresh user input restored reclaimed compute
Navigating to another scene or out of the course stopped activity reports
All live test environments were confirmed destroyed after the scenarios
During development, live tools exposed maintenance lock contention and an old-message retry deadline; both have real-PG regressions, and the fresh real-model turn succeeded after fixes
limitations: Cloud verification uses a small Python workspace, one browser scenario and local object storage; concurrent capacity and production object-storage latency are not measured
Unexpected provider or application failure can lose changes since the last successful checkpoint; periodic dirty checkpoints require no active managed writer

After the configured idle archive-failure grace, release may discard changes newer than the last successful checkpoint; a durable loss notice identifies the recoverable version. If control metadata cannot be saved, provider-lease expiry is the compute fallback.

findingsAddressed: Bound permanently unknown overdue commands using the idle failure grace even when cancellation cannot be acknowledged
Preserve the actual destroyed state while fencing discard-intent writes
Use the same resolved failure stage in diagnostics and durable metadata
